recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: Employee + LeavePolicy + Audit
recommended_phases.rationale: These three modules have zero dependencies on other leave modules. Employee provides identity/manager lookups. LeavePolicy defines leave types and entitlement rules. Audit is the cross-cutting audit record sink required by GP-002. Build them first so every subsequent phase can depend on them.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — LeaveBalance
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on Phase 1 (Employee + LeavePolicy + Audit). Provides balance tracking, deduction, restoration, and initialization. Must exist before LeaveRequest can deduct/restore balances during approval/rejection/cancellation flows.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Notification
recommended_phases.rationale: Standalone module with no dependencies on other leave modules. Can be built in parallel with Phase 2, but placed here so LeaveRequest can wire notifications for status changes. Sends leave-status-change notifications to employees and managers.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — LeaveRequest (core orchestration)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all prior phases. Orchestrates the full leave-request lifecycle: submit (validates policy, checks balance, creates request, audits), approve/reject (updates status, deducts/restores balance, audits, notifies), cancel (restores balance, audits, notifies). This is the largest module and the integration point.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries

- **Presentation**: Fastify route handlers in each module's `*.routes.ts` — validate inputs (GP-003), enforce RBAC (GP-005), delegate to service interfaces.
- **Application**: Service interfaces + implementations — orchestrate business logic, call repositories, enforce transaction boundaries, emit audit records (GP-002).
- **Domain**: Models (LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, LeavePolicy, Employee, AuditLog, Notification) — pure data structures, enums (LeaveStatus, LeaveType), DTOs.
- **Infrastructure**: Repositories (one per aggregate), PostgreSQL via `pg` Pool from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`, base repository pattern from `src/shared/`.

## Dependency direction (inward only)

```
leave-request ──► leave-balance ──► leave-policy
     │                │
     │                ├──► employee
     │                │
     ├──► leave-policy │
     ├──► employee     │
     ├──► audit ◄──────┘
     └──► notification
```

No module depends on leave-request. No cycles exist.

## Key design decisions

- **LeaveRequestService** orchestrates the full lifecycle: `submitLeaveRequest` validates policy via LeavePolicyService, checks active employment via EmployeeService, then persists. `approveLeaveRequest` deducts balance via LeaveBalanceService, records audit, sends notification. `rejectLeaveRequest` and `cancelLeaveRequest` restore balance when applicable.
- **LeaveBalanceService** owns balance arithmetic: `deductBalance` and `restoreBalance` are called by LeaveRequestService during state transitions, never directly from routes.
- **AuditService** is a cross-cutting dependency — every state-changing operation in leave-request and leave-balance writes an audit record (GP-002).
- **NotificationService** is fire-and-forget from the application layer; failures are logged but do not roll back the business transaction.
- **RBAC** is enforced at the route/controller layer (GP-005): employees can only submit/cancel their own requests; managers can only approve/reject requests from their team members (verified via EmployeeService.getTeamMembers).
